title: Major Saudi conferences to proceed, organisers say, despite deadly airport attack
gist: Reuters via Al-Monitor: organisers of the World Petroleum Congress (Oct 11-15) and the Future Investment Initiative (Oct 26-29) said both Riyadh events will go ahead with tighter security, despite Houthi missile attacks on Riyadh's airport that killed four, disrupted flights and led the UK, France and Germany to warn citizens away from the city.

insights.claim: Riyadh is sticking to plans to host global events and attract investment even as its escalating war with the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen has seen the kingdom attacked dozens of times in recent weeks.
insights.so_what: Saudi Arabia is prioritising investor confidence and Vision-style dealmaking over caution, but security risk now sits inside the capital.
insights.quote: Riyadh is sticking to plans to convene global events and trying to draw in investment even amid escalating war with the Iran-backed Houthis in neighbouring Yemen
insights.locator: Riyadh is sticking to plans to
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: Organisers of the World Petroleum Congress, hosting top global oil executives and policymakers from Sunday to Thursday, told delegates it would proceed as planned with foreign leaders and ministers attending, and suggested a four-hour drive from Dammam as an alternative route to Riyadh.
insights.so_what: Logistics workarounds show the airport disruption is material even as Riyadh projects normality.
insights.quote: alternative routes to Riyadh, including via a four-hour drive from Dammam on the kingdom's eastern coast, were available
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: The Future Investment Initiative, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's flagship investment conference, will still run October 26-29, with comprehensive security at Riyadh's airports, venues and official hotels, according to FII CEO Maha Al Saud.
insights.so_what: FII attendance will be a visible test of global capital's willingness to engage with Saudi Arabia under fire.
insights.quote: Comprehensive security measures will be in place at Riyadh's airports, our conference venues and official hotels, with coordinated arrangements for participants' transportation,
insights.locator: Safety and well-being remain our highest
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon and Citi CEO Jane Fraser were among expected attendees at the Future Investment Initiative.
insights.so_what: Whether top Wall Street CEOs attend in person will signal how much security risk global finance tolerates for Saudi deal flow.
insights.quote: Chief executives of some of the world's biggest financial institutions such as JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon and Citi's Jane Fraser were on the list of expected attendees.
insights.locator: Chief executives of some of the
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: Italian Energy Minister Gilberto Pichetto Fratin said he would not fly to Riyadh for the International Energy Forum Ministerial Meeting and would join by video link instead.
insights.so_what: Early sign that senior foreign officials are cutting in-person attendance despite organisers' assurances.
insights.locator: Italian Energy Minister Gilberto Pichetto Fratin
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: Missile attacks on Riyadh's airport this week killed four people, heavily damaged an airliner, and caused widespread flight disruption, with travellers using land routes or roundabout alternative flights.
insights.so_what: Disruption to the capital's main air gateway hits business travel, tourism and airline revenues.
insights.quote: The attacks led to widespread flight disruptions, with people taking land routes or circuitous alternative flights.
insights.locator: The attacks led to widespread flight
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: The UK, France and Germany warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh.
insights.so_what: Western travel advisories can deter expatriate staffing and corporate visits, and complicate insurance.
insights.quote: The UK, France and Germany have warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh.
insights.locator: The attacks led to widespread flight
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: Lufthansa suspended Riyadh flights through October 16, while Gulf carriers Etihad Airways and Flydubai cancelled October 10 flights to and from the Saudi capital.
insights.so_what: Airline suspensions are a direct revenue hit and a gauge of how commercial operators price the security risk.
insights.quote: Germany's Lufthansa has suspended Riyadh flights through October 16
insights.locator: Germany's Lufthansa has suspended Riyadh flights
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: The Houthis declared Saudi airspace a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against them earlier in the month.
insights.so_what: Links the aviation threat directly to the Yemen ground offensive, so it lasts as long as that campaign.
insights.locator: The Houthis have said airliners should
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia has answered Houthi attacks with waves of strikes on missile launcher sites and says it has intercepted many ballistic missiles fired by the group.
insights.so_what: Points to a continuing strike-counterstrike cycle rather than a quick end to the threat.
insights.locator: Saudi Arabia has responded to Houthi
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
